text: A well-designed REST API is a pleasure to use. First, keep your endpoints clear and logical, such as `/users` or `/orders`, so developers can easily guess the structure. Always use standard HTTP status codes—like 200 for success, 404 for not found, and 500 for server errors—so clients can react appropriately. Good documentation is essential; it should explain each endpoint, its parameters, and example responses. Finally, never break existing clients when you make changes. Instead, use versioning, for example by prefixing your URL with `/v1/` or `/v2/`. This way, you can add new features while old integrations continue to work smoothly. Following these practices saves time and frustration for everyone.
